paras: Gamut Golf makes headcovers out of things that already existed, and the sourcing is what sets it apart. The baseball covers are cut from authentic vintage jerseys, several of them marked 1 of 1. The course covers are cut from genuine course towels from Shinnecock, Pebble Beach, the Old Course, Sawgrass and Pinehurst. Because the cloth is finite, most of the interesting pieces can never be made twice.

The details are unusually specific. One cover is built from a Mirage Cooperstown Collection throwback carrying a team name retired decades ago. A Muirfield Village cover is lined with deadstock Ralph Lauren suit liner, and the Richard Pouch uses rare deadstock Double RL. Next to the covers sit hardwood alignment sticks at $98, a solid brass divot tool, waxed canvas pouches and a set of walnut brushes.

The catalog is small, about 35 products, and most of the one-off covers sell out fast. Prices run from $22 to $128. Gamut suits the golfer who wants one object in the bag nobody else can order, and the alignment sticks are the sleeper pick. We first profiled the brand in September 2026 and included the sticks in our alignment stick edit.
faq: What does Gamut Golf make?
One-of-one golf headcovers cut from authentic vintage baseball jerseys and genuine course towels, plus hardwood alignment sticks, a brass divot tool, waxed canvas pouches and walnut brushes.
How much do Gamut Golf headcovers cost?
The catalog runs from $22 to $128. A cover cut from a vintage throwback jersey sits at the top of that range, and the hardwood alignment sticks are $98.
Why do Gamut Golf covers sell out?
Each cover is cut from a single jersey or towel, so many pieces are marked 1 of 1 and cannot be remade once sold.

paras: Fyfe Golf makes headcovers that come from somewhere specific. Every cover is cut, lined and sewn to order in a workshop in Fife, Scotland, in Harris Tweed, Scottish tartan and waxed canvas from Dundee. Several times a year the material is something that used to be a different object entirely: an RAF flight suit, a caddie's coverall from Augusta, a deck chair or the sail cloth off a yacht on the west coast.

Neil Rennie started Fyfe in November 2021 after years of walking into Scottish pro shops and finding nothing in them that had anything to do with Scotland. He came out of fashion rather than golf, so he already knew which mills still wove cloth and how to reach them. Fyfe names its mills, which is rarer than it sounds. The Arran Harris Tweed cover at £65 (~$87) is the everyday version of the idea.

The Harris Tweed covers are the reason to know the brand, the tartans are the ones people ask about, and the reclaimed runs are where it gets interesting. Those usually sell out inside a week. Fyfe has also made a long run of collaborations with MacKenzie, the Oregon bag maker, and it appears on our 25 Best Independent Golf Brands list.
faq: Where are Fyfe Golf headcovers made?
In Fyfe's own workshop in Fife, Scotland, where every cover is cut, lined and sewn to order.
Who founded Fyfe Golf?
Neil Rennie, who launched the brand in November 2021 after a career in fashion.
What materials does Fyfe Golf use?
Harris Tweed, Scottish tartan and waxed canvas from Dundee, plus limited runs cut from reclaimed material such as RAF flight suits, Augusta caddie coveralls and yacht sail cloth.

paras: RIPIT treats the golf grip as the last unclaimed surface on a club, and prints art on it. The brand is Australian, and founder Todd Watts spent three years getting a print to survive the molding process before he sold a single grip. The result is artwork worked into the surface of the rubber rather than laid on top.

Every RIPIT grip carries an alignment mark at both ends. The brand releases in limited art series the way an apparel label runs drops. The Eldrick, a deep oxblood grip with a line drawing in the surface, is the one we picked out at $24.95.

A full set is thirteen grips, so a RIPIT set comes to about $325, which is why most golfers start with one club. We covered RIPIT in our Niche Grip Report alongside four other independent grip makers, as one of two brands treating the grip as a canvas for print.
faq: Where is RIPIT Grips from?
Australia. The brand was founded by Todd Watts.
How much are RIPIT golf grips?
Single grips are around $25; the Eldrick was $24.95 when we checked. A full set of thirteen comes to about $325.
Do RIPIT grips have alignment marks?
Yes. Every RIPIT grip has an alignment mark at both ends.

paras: Read The Green makes good golf hats first, and everything else has had to earn its place. The New York brand began as three words shouted at a buddy who missed the pin on a miniature golf course, and four lifelong friends turned the joke into a hat and apparel label that moves between the course and the city without a costume change.

The Founder's Cap at $47 is the signature: a five-panel corduroy cap with embroidered details and a custom interior lining most people never see. The '97 Vintage Pullover is the piece that put RTG on the map, a lightweight nylon layer with rib-knit cuffs and a drawstring waist. The Grounds Crew Jacket and an oversized knit sweater push the line upmarket, while the Varsity Crewneck and Club Tee keep it accessible.

Prices run from $40 to $150. Cody Bellinger, Jasson Domínguez and Lexie Hull all wear it, but the brand still feels like it belongs to the weekend golfer who cares what he puts on. We profiled Read The Green in our Brand to Know series and included it in our jersey polo edit.
faq: Where is Read The Green based?
New York. The brand was started by four lifelong friends.
What is Read The Green known for?
Golf hats, led by the five-panel corduroy Founder's Cap, and the '97 Vintage Pullover, the nylon layer that went viral.
How much does Read The Green cost?
The range runs from $40 to $150, with the Founder's Cap at $47.

paras: AXXA makes golf clothes for someone who surfs in the morning and plays after lunch, and the photography backs that up: the same jumper appears on a fairway at golden hour and on a clifftop above the break. The brand was born on Sydney's Northern Beaches in 2022, and its own line is that it was "founded in 2022 by then 14-year-old Axel".

The surf half explains the clothes. A brand that only thinks about golf makes polos and caps and stops. AXXA makes heavyweight jacquard knitwear, up to 980g, with the graphic knitted in rather than printed on, plus a canvas workwear jacket and its own GolfComfort polo fabric. The knits are the most interesting thing it makes, and the reason is construction rather than design.

The catalog is 18 pieces, priced from A$59 to A$169 (about $39 to $112). It suits the golfer who wants coastal clothes that work on the first tee and at the pub after. We profiled AXXA in September 2026 in our Brand to Know series.
faq: Where is AXXA from?
Sydney's Northern Beaches, Australia. The brand started in 2022.
What does AXXA make?
Golf and coastal apparel: heavyweight jacquard knitwear, polos in its own GolfComfort fabric, caps and a canvas workwear jacket.
How much does AXXA cost?
Prices run from A$59 to A$169, roughly $39 to $112.

paras: Daphne's Headcovers invented the animal headcover, and it made the most famous one in golf. The Phoenix company was founded in 1979 by Jane Spicer and her mother, Daphne. Frank, the tiger, went on Tiger Woods' driver at the 1997 Masters, Nike licensed the character and named him, and the business grew 400% in a quarter.

Spicer's one condition for the licensing deal was that Frank stay likable. Her late mother's actual signature is stitched into the label of every cover the company makes, which says a lot about how the family thinks of the business more than four decades on.

The range is more than a hundred animal designs at a flat $45.99, from wolf and shark to Jack Nicklaus's Golden Bear. Daphne's suits the golfer who wants a cover with a sense of humor and a real piece of golf history behind it. We included the brand in our guide to golf brands founded by women.
faq: Who made Tiger Woods' tiger headcover?
Daphne's Headcovers of Phoenix made Frank, the tiger cover Tiger Woods carried at the 1997 Masters.
When was Daphne's Headcovers founded?
In 1979, by Jane Spicer and her mother, Daphne.
How much are Daphne's headcovers?
More than a hundred animal designs sell at a flat $45.99.

paras: Après Golf sells provenance you cannot order twice. The covers are hi-loft sherpa fleece, hand-sewn in a California factory that has been running since 1992, but the reason people stop you on the tee is the patch on the front: Chamonix, St. Moritz, Alta, Mad River Glen, cut off ski jackets someone wore somewhere before they got near a golf bag.

The name comes from après-ski, the part of a ski day after the skiing. Après buys vintage ski-resort and country-club patches, cuts fleece around them and sells the result to golfers. In its own words: "We source vintage patches, create new patches, embroider logos and print custom designs." The tie-dye prints are the ones people ask about, and the vintage patches are the ones that will not be repeatable.

The catalog runs to about fifty pieces across eight groups, from $38 to $138, and the Fruit Looper at $88 is the clearest version of the idea. There is also a custom program where you post them a patch of your own. We profiled Après Golf in September 2026.
faq: Where are Après Golf headcovers made?
Hand-sewn in a California factory that has been running since 1992.
What are Après Golf headcovers made of?
Hi-loft sherpa fleece, with vintage ski-resort and country-club patches, new patches, embroidery or custom prints on the front.
How much does Après Golf cost?
Pieces run from $38 to $138; most patched sherpa covers are around $88.

paras: MacKenzie has made one thing by hand in Oregon since 1985: the carry bag. PGA Tour pro Peter Jacobsen and his brother David started the company and named it after Rick MacKenzie, the St Andrews caddie who once carried double for them by tipping both their staff bags into a single leather pencil bag. The first logo was a drawing lifted off his business card.

Forty years on, it is a very small company with a very long order book, with ten employees, seven of whom actually make bags. The house style is consistent: an eight-inch top, a single strap, one pocket if you are lucky, and full-grain leather or waxed canvas built to order in your colors.

MacKenzie is also the maker other brands go to when they want an object rather than a product. It has built bags for Fyfe Golf, Sugarloaf Social Club, Miura and Bandon Dunes, among many others, most of them sold through the partner rather than MacKenzie itself. We collected that record in our MacKenzie Collab Archive, and MacKenzie appears on our 25 Best Independent Golf Brands list.
faq: Where are MacKenzie golf bags made?
By hand in Oregon, where the company has built carry bags since 1985.
Who is MacKenzie named after?
Rick MacKenzie, a St Andrews caddie who carried for founders Peter and David Jacobsen.
Does MacKenzie make custom bags?
Yes. The classic Mac is built to order in your choice of leather or waxed canvas and colors, and MacKenzie also makes collaboration bags for other brands and clubs.

paras: Agronomy Workshop behaves like a designer who happens to have made golf clothes, which is exactly what it is. The San Francisco brand launched in October 2025, but founder Rob Junge had been collecting for it for four and a half years before that, in a public moodboard he started in May 2021 and still adds to.

Junge is a working creative director whose career runs through product design at Vimeo, independent design practice in San Francisco and Head of Design at a sports streaming startup. The clothes show it. The signature is a heavyweight cotton work shirt with a hidden tee slot, alongside rope hats and towels. The whole operation reads like a greenkeeper who reads design blogs: practical first, considered second and loud about neither.

The range is small, about a dozen pieces, and built around cotton rather than performance synthetics. It suits the golfer who wants a shirt that looks like a work shirt and happens to hold a tee. We covered Agronomy Workshop in our Brand Revisited series and included it in our tee and towel edits.
faq: Where is Agronomy Workshop based?
San Francisco, California. The brand launched in October 2025.
Who founded Agronomy Workshop?
Rob Junge, a creative director and product designer.
What is Agronomy Workshop known for?
A heavyweight cotton golf work shirt with a hidden tee slot, plus rope hats and golf towels.

paras: Aimé Leon Dore treats golf as if it had always been part of New York street culture. The Queens label, founded by Teddy Santis in 2014, makes menswear, footwear and accessories, and has released a golf collection every spring since 2024.

The SS26 capsule, which dropped on April 23, was the most complete yet. The headliner was the ALD x FootJoy Premiere Series Marquis in croc-embossed leather at $375, waterproof, in two colorways. Blackwatch plaid ran through a Tips windbreaker at $495 and a Cordura pullover at $295, and the merino Clubhouse Sweater at $395 carried an intarsia golfer on the chest. A leather-and-Cordura putter cover, performance socks, a flask and a cigar lighter rounded it out.
Prices run from $40 to $495. ALD suits the golfer who wants clubhouse prep with a New York edge. We have covered its SS26 golf releases and included its socks in our sock edit.
faq: Does Aimé Leon Dore make golf clothes?
Yes. ALD releases a golf capsule each spring; the SS26 collection dropped on April 23, 2026.
Who founded Aimé Leon Dore?
Teddy Santis, in Queens, New York, in 2014.
How much is the Aimé Leon Dore golf collection?
The SS26 golf pieces ran from $40 to $495, including the ALD x FootJoy Premiere Series Marquis at $375.
